title: Phasor and Impedance Visualiser
scope: A series or parallel RLC circuit driven by an ideal sinusoidal voltage source, in sinusoidal steady state: impedance and admittance, element voltages or branch currents as phasors, waveforms, real, reactive and apparent power, resonance and quality factor. Ideal components only; no sweeps, transients, source impedance or three-phase.
conventions: Imaginary unit j; amplitudes are RMS; the source voltage is the reference at 0 degrees.
Angles in degrees, positive counter-clockwise, normalised to (-180, 180].
phi = arg Z. phi > 0 is inductive (current lags voltage); phi < 0 is capacitive (current leads). The current phasor is at -phi.
Series: Z = R + j(omega L - 1/(omega C)). Parallel: Y = 1/R + j(omega C - 1/(omega L)), Z = 1/Y. An element switched off is absent (removed from the loop or its branch removed).
P = V I cos phi, Q = V I sin phi (positive inductive), S = V I, power factor = cos phi, lagging when inductive and leading when capacitive.
f0 = 1/(2 pi sqrt(LC)) when L and C are both on; quality factor Q_f = omega0 L / R (series) or R / (omega0 L) (parallel) when R, L and C are all on.
v(t) = sqrt(2) V sin(omega t), i(t) = sqrt(2) I sin(omega t - phi); waveforms are drawn per unit of their own peak.
Canonical units in every file: ohm, H, F, Hz, V (RMS), degrees.
degenerate: Series with L and C on and R off at f0 (|Z| < 1e-9 ohm): current, element voltages, S and Q are unbounded; phi and the power factor are undefined.
Parallel with L and C on and R off at f0 (|Y| < 1e-12 S): impedance unbounded, total current 0; phi and the power factor are undefined.
Only one element on: f0, Q_f and the resonance comparison read 'needs L and C'.
sources: Standard steady-state AC circuit analysis, as in C. K. Alexander and M. N. O. Sadiku, Fundamentals of Electric Circuits, chapters 9 to 11 and 14.
